title: Detailed cellular automaton properties correlate with the four classes

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Detailed cellular automaton properties correlate with the four classes

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Most detailed properties of cellular automata correlate closely with the four visually defined classes, so that knowing a cellular automaton's class is often enough to predict its detailed properties.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: most of these properties were closely correlated with the classes that I had already identified. Indeed, in trying to predict detailed properties of a particular cellular automaton, it was often enough just to know what class the cellular automaton was in.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 6, “Starting from Randomness”; section “Four Classes of Behavior” (from p. 231), p. 235. Scope: cellular automata in general

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch06-04: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.61

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A noncircular predictive analysis is feasible for selected properties and rule families. The quantifier over most properties and cellular automata is too open-ended for complete resolution.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Define a list of detailed properties independently of class labels, classify a large rule sample blindly, and measure cross-validated predictive accuracy from class to each property. Compare against rule-level and trivial baseline predictors.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Coverage across cellular automata is incomplete.

Classes may be assigned using the same properties, creating circularity.

“Most detailed properties” has no enumerated universe.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.42
discriminating power: 0.55
analysis feasibility: 0.66
data existence: 0.88
data adequacy: 0.48

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Standard cellular-automaton statistics are cheap to compute for elementary rules, and association with a pre-registered class label is an ordinary analysis. The sentence says most properties and often enough, and it is easy to build a circular test that reuses the visual features as both label and outcome. A held-out statistic can support the correlation on a finite family only.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Assign classes from one declared criterion, then predict held-out measurements such as damage-spread rate, cycle growth with ring size, and language size. High mutual information supports the correlation; a property that stays unpredictable after the class is known challenges it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A property used to assign the class cannot be counted as an independent prediction.

Most detailed properties is an open list.

Borderline rules, which the text displays, weaken a strict correlation.
